version.changelog: Clarify Playwright install workflow and CLI auth-file help

llm.summary: The skill's code, requested installs, and runtime instructions are consistent with a Shanghai Library seat-booking CLI that uses Playwright for browser-assisted login and the library's API; nothing appears to request unrelated credentials or contact unexpected endpoints.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (seat booking for Shanghai Library East Branch 3F) matches the code and instructions: CLI commands to list/cancel/book/scan availability, Playwright-based browser login to extract accessToken/sign/timestamp, and HTTP calls to yuyue.library.sh.cn. Required binaries (node/npm/npx) and the Playwright dependency are expected for this functionality.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and scripts only instruct operations needed for booking: open browser for manual login, extract and save auth fields to local profile files, call the library API endpoints, and download Chromium for Playwright. The runtime code reads/writes profile files under the user config dir and does not reference unrelated system paths or attempt to exfiltrate data to domains other than the library's endpoints.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Registry install metadata provides a brew formula for Node.js on macOS. The README/SKILL.md instruct users to run `npm install` and `npx playwright install chromium`, which will download npm packages and a Chromium binary from upstream sources. This is expected for a Playwright-based tool but does mean external downloads and disk writes occur during setup; the brew-only install spec may be incomplete for non-macOS environments.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables or unrelated credentials. Authentication is managed via local profile files (default ~/.config/shlibrary-seat-booking/profiles/*.json) containing accessToken/sign/timestamp; those are appropriate for the library API and are read/written by the tool. No other service tokens or secrets are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not force-included (always: false) and does not modify other skills or global agent settings. It stores auth files in a user-scoped config directory and may launch a browser session to capture/refresh tokens, which is normal for this function. It does not request elevated system privileges.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do exactly what it says: automate browser-assisted login (manual entry of credentials/CAPTCHA) to extract auth tokens and then call the Shanghai Library booking API. Before installing/using it, note: (1) setup requires running `npm install` and `npx playwright install chromium` which will download code and a Chromium binary from upstream; run these in a trusted, non-root environment; (2) the tool will read and write auth files in ~/.config/shlibrary-seat-booking/profiles/*.json — protect these files (e.g., chmod 600) because they contain tokens; (3) the login flow opens a browser and extracts accessToken/sign/timestamp — ensure you trust the code (review login.js) if you will enter credentials; (4) the registry install only includes a brew node formula for macOS — on Linux/Windows you must install Node.js and npm yourself. If any of these behaviors are unacceptable, review the scripts (especially scripts/login.js and scripts/login_and_get_auth_node.js) before running.
